# Reading policy for the reference kernel (fixed by the orchestrator; every item is reported for arbitration)

General
- The frozen spec specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md is the only semantic source. Cite clauses as §N or §N.k (item k).
- Formalize each clause as written. Never add a clause the text does not state (no "robustness"); never drop one.
- When a clause has no checkable content in the state (undefined term), do not invent content: omit it from the definition and record it in readings.md (clause, quote, why it cannot be formalized).
- When a clause has two readings, use the one listed below; if the case is not listed, use the draft's reading if the draft matches one of the readings, and record it in readings.md with both readings and an example of a program whose verdict changes.
- A representation choice that changes no accepted program is free (record it briefly).

State (§38): S3 = (F, nF, P, I, A, D, dead, pin). No arena registry, no callParams, no freed. Library state lives elsewhere.
Outcomes (§58): one type Outcome3 σ := ok σ | reject | fail; every O1–O16 relation except alloc never yields fail.
O1 derive (§60): takes a region (List Nat, read extensionally), not a place. Preconditions: active source; ExercisableAt source mode; every leaf of region exists, is a leaf, belongs to afp source; mode ≤ effective mode of source on each leaf; §60.3 as a decidable clause (no unrelated active authority becomes incompatible); §60.4 current frame live. §60.1c "origin chain and anchors valid" and §60.4b "footprint and anchoring restrictions": no checkable content -> omitted, recorded.
O2 split (§61): draft clauses (incl. no exclusive right already distributed). §61.4 is NOT a precondition (the §61 note says an accepted split may violate I1 without DDSound) -> recorded.
O3 release (§62): draft clauses; §62.5 (abstraction contracts) omitted, recorded.
O4 transfer (§63): draft clauses MINUS the draft's extra clause "(transferEff s src dst).Usable dst" (not in §63); PLUS §63.8 (local self-blocking prevention, as LockOptions.Opt2Transfer on formal/derivability_0.1); effect: dependencies follow the corresponding places corr(r) (not all to the destination root); §63.6 over moved usable places and AnchorOrder in the resulting state; §63.7 AnchorOrderHeld for the moved held authorities in the resulting state; §63.4 = draft ActiveDerivedOutside reading (recorded); §63.2 child order = place index order (recorded).
O5 depend (§64): draft clauses; §64.2b "real dependency" omitted, recorded.
O8 store (§65): draft clauses (they match).
O9/O10/O11 (§66–§68): add "every leaf belongs to a usable place" (§66.1, §67.1, §68.1); O10 keeps §67.2 explicitly.
O12 endUse (§69): death markers transitive over owned storage; drop the draft's extra disjunct that blocks descendants of authorities the step releases (not in §69.2) -> record the consequence.
O13 free (§70): death markers transitive; no extra "Usable p" and no clearing of D beyond what §70 prescribes; §70.4 scope = the released unit (place and storage that dies with it).
O14 alloc (§71): shape nonempty with exactly ONE root (one new storage root), parts' parents inside the shape, no owner component; provider clause as written in §71.2 (Modify OR writeShared over SharedMutable metadata) -> conflict with §36 recorded; outcomes reject / fail (not Satisfiable) / ok.
O6 enterFrame (§72): locals owned directly by the new frame (no local owned by another local); §72.3 ParamOriginHidden; §72.4 AnchorOrderHeld in the resulting state.
O7 exitFrame (§73): draft (first surviving active origin, held by a frame or a usable place).
O15/O16 pin/unpin (§74, §75): per-leaf dynamic pin flags (draft); unpin requires the place usable and K.ExternalDone(place) on the place; StaticPinnedBottom is a condition on (K, statics), not on states.
HasRight / ExercisableAt (§43): one authority exercisable at m with sufficient effective mode on every leaf (∃ a, ∀ l) as the draft -> recorded.
WF3 (§49): a structure with eight named fields, one per item:
 1 frames: F nonempty, no duplicates, every frame < nF;
 2 places: parent links valid and acyclic (representation: parent index < child index), parts share the owner and death marker of their parent;
 3 owners: owner frames < nF, owner places exist; "well-founded ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place" read as stated for usable places (Usable is inductive) -> recorded with the global-acyclicity alternative;
 4 footprints: every footprint member is an existing leaf;
 5 authorities: origins exist and precede (origin index < id: representation of acyclic chains ending at a root);
 6 RootChain (draft);
 7 RootHeld as §49.7 states it: every usable root place has an active root authority, Modify, no origin, held by its owner, whose footprint is the place's footprint (draft RootLive + mode);
 8 holder validity (draft poss).
 The draft's converse RootHeld (every origin-less authority covering a leaf of root r is held by r's owner) is NOT a WF3 clause: keep it as a separate auxiliary predicate.
I2 (§51): mode conservation unconditional (not under ∀ p ∈ footprint).
Initial state (§47): base frame 0; statics may be owned by statics; root authority held by the owner. Well-formedness of the statics declaration (acyclic ownership, parents before children) is not stated by §47: keep the draft ShapeOK-style hypothesis as a hypothesis of the init theorems and record it as a spec gap.
Reachable: closure of S3.init statics under the kernel steps O1–O16 only.

186:**Principe.** Un handle est une donnée ; il ne porte aucune autorité. La résolution fournit un accès temporaire de seconde classe. # ERN — Jalon 3 : matériel pour revue unique

**Objet :** validation adversariale du Memory Model (spec 1) après les jalons 1 et 2.
**Contenu :** les trois corpus mis à jour, le contrat du pool de handles, le cadrage de la décision `NoLock`, le registre des obligations inter-spécifications.

## 0. Règles du jalon 3

1. **Oracle indépendant.** Le verdict attendu d'un cas vient de sa source (clause de MM-02 v0.4, de MM-03.3 v0.3, arbitrage, ou usage déclaré), jamais du comportement des modules. Un cas sans source qui tranche est marqué « à arbitrer ».
2. **Jumeau positif.** Chaque rejet a un jumeau minimal accepté : même séquence sans l'élément fautif. Un rejet qui persiste dans le jumeau est un défaut de construction.
3. **États atteints.** Chaque cas est construit depuis l'état initial par des pas autorisés.
4. **Pas de correction silencieuse.** Un verdict obtenu différent de l'attendu est rapporté avec l'état et le pas en cause.
5. **Classement.** Chaque cas relève de : noyau MM-03 (`N3`), machine MM-02 (`N2`), raffinement (`R`), instance de bibliothèque (`Lib` : arène, pool), ou d'une autre spécification (spec 2, 3, 4, 11). Les cas d'une autre spécification restent des obligations inter-spécifications ; ils ne bloquent pas la clôture du jalon 3.
6. **Couverture.** La colonne « Couvert » indique un témoin déjà produit pendant les jalons 1 et 2, quand il est identifié avec certitude. Le jalon 3 rejoue tous les cas depuis l'état initial, couverts ou non, dans un module de cas séparé.
7. **Cible des corpus.** MM3-H et MM23-H sont encodés au jalon 3 sur les brouillons, sans modifier `MM02`, `MM03` ni `MM23`. MM2-H : ses verdicts sont révisés au jalon 3, mais sa validation exécutable reste une obligation de la reconstruction de référence ; le jalon 3 ne le déclare pas validé.
8. **Écarts connus.** Un cas dont le verdict attendu repose sur une décision non encore appliquée au brouillon (MM23-H15, H16) est encodé avec le verdict obtenu, marqué « écart connu », et inscrit au registre de reconstruction. Il n'est jamais présenté comme réussi.

| ID | Scénario | Attendu | Source | Classe | Couvert |

---

## 4. Contrat du pool de handles (instance de bibliothèque, comme l'arène)

**Principe.** Un handle est une donnée ; il ne porte aucune autorité. La résolution fournit un accès temporaire de seconde classe. Aucun drapeau d'emprunt par entrée : l'exclusivité d'une résolution `Modify` découle des règles du noyau (I1, O3.2), par la forme de l'arbre de dérivation ci-dessous.

**État de l'entrée de pool** (abstrait, comme l'entrée d'arène ; sa représentation en octets est une obligation de l'implémentation) : `{id, storage, internal, slots}`.
- `id` : identité de pool fraîche à chaque `newPool`, jamais réutilisée pendant l'exécution. Un pool détruit puis recréé, même sur le même stockage, a une autre identité.
- `slots` : chaque entrée est `{place, gen : Nat, live : Bool}` ; `place` est une partie de `storage`.
- La valeur pool est le détenteur de `internal` (même règle que F1). Le stockage peut être local, statique, alloué ou un bloc.

**Handle** : `(id, slot, gen)`, une donnée de taille fixe.

**Emprunt composé.** Une résolution est un emprunt composé : une autorité **compagne** dérivée de `internal` sur **tout le stockage** du pool, au mode de la résolution, détenue par le cadre courant ; puis une autorité d'**entrée** par handle résolu, dérivée **de la compagne** (sous-empreinte), au même mode, détenue par le cadre courant et étiquetée de la génération résolue. Conséquences, toutes par les règles existantes du noyau :
- la compagne ne peut être libérée tant qu'une de ses autorités d'entrée est active (O3.2) ;
- une compagne `Modify` active rend le mode effectif de `internal` absent sur tout le stockage : toute nouvelle résolution, `Modify` ou `Observe`, est rejetée, quels que soient les handles ;
- plusieurs compagnes `Observe` coexistent ; une résolution `Modify` est alors rejetée.

**Opérations**

- **`newPool storage internal`** : préconditions de `newArena` (F1, F2, J1) ; identité fraîche ; toutes les entrées libres, générations à 0.
- **`allocSlot pool dst : ok | fail | reject`** : droit de mise à jour sur la valeur pool (`Modify` exerçable ou `writeShared` sur métadonnées `SharedMutable`) ; `dst` est une feuille non `Init`, ne détenant aucune autorité active, de la taille d'un handle, `Modify` exerçable ; `fail` si aucune entrée libre (état inchangé) ; `ok` : une entrée libre devient vivante, son contenu reste `Uninit`, le handle `(id, slot, gen)` est écrit dans `dst`, qui seule passe à `Init`.
- **`resolve h m : ok | fail | reject`** (`m` = `Observe` ou `Modify`) : droit d'exercice de `internal` au mode `m` par la valeur pool ; les vérifications d'identité et de génération lisent seulement les métadonnées et précèdent toute création d'autorité ; `fail` (état inchangé) si `h.id` n'est pas l'identité du pool, si `h.gen` diffère de la génération de l'entrée, ou si l'entrée est libre ; `ok` : emprunt composé à une entrée. Une compagne déjà active n'est jamais réutilisée : chaque résolution crée la sienne.
- **`resolveMany hs m : ok | fail | reject`** : une compagne, une autorité d'entrée par handle (par `split` de la compagne) ; `fail` si un handle est périmé ou d'un autre pool, ou si deux handles désignent la même entrée ; **atomique** : en cas de `fail`, aucune autorité n'est créée. Coût dynamique explicite : vérification de distinction proportionnelle au lot. C'est la voie des requêtes ECS.
- **`unresolve`** : `release` des autorités d'entrée, puis de la compagne.
- **`freeSlot h : ok | fail | reject`** : droit de mise à jour sur la valeur pool ; `fail` si `h` est périmé ou d'un autre pool ; `reject` si une autorité active dérivée de `internal` couvre l'entrée (donc pendant toute résolution du pool, puisque chaque compagne couvre tout le stockage) ; sinon fin logique du contenu de l'entrée **selon `endUse`** (mêmes préconditions : aucune dépendance utilisable, aucune feuille épinglée ; mêmes effets : feuilles `Uninit`, autorités détenues libérées, dépendances supprimées, stockage possédé logiquement mort, sans désallocation) — `reject` si une précondition d'`endUse` échoue ; une entrée déjà `Uninit` est acceptée ; puis l'entrée devient libre et sa génération est incrémentée.

**Invariant `PoolInv`** (tout pool vivant) : entrées deux à deux disjointes et incluses dans le stockage ; toute autorité active dérivée d'une compagne du pool sur une entrée porte la génération courante de l'entrée, et l'entrée est vivante ; toute compagne active a au plus les autorités d'entrée de sa résolution pour descendants.

**Générations et identités** : `Nat` dans le modèle ; le débordement des générations et l'unicité réelle des identités de pool sont des obligations de l'implémentation, classées bibliothèque et spec 11.

**Théorèmes attendus**
- `pool_resolve_stale_fails`, `pool_resolve_other_pool_fails` ;
- `pool_no_stale_access` : aucune autorité active d'une génération périmée ;
- `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive` : sur tout état atteint, au plus une compagne `Modify` active par pool, et alors aucune compagne `Observe` — quelle que soit la séquence de `resolve`, `resolveMany`, `release`, `store`, `transfer` et `unresolve` qui y mène ;
- `pool_resolveMany_atomic` et `pool_resolveMany_distinct` ;
- `pool_freeSlot_ends_content` : après `freeSlot`, le contenu de l'entrée satisfait les effets d'`endUse` ;
- `pool_inv_preserved`, et intégration à `Reachable` dans un module séparé, noyau inchangé.

**Cas** : H30–H34b, H44, W1.

## 5. Décision `NoLock` — cadrage

**Fait établi (passe 7).** Des états atteints contiennent des autorités détenues que personne ne peut exercer, ce qui bloque un `reset` ou un `free` jusqu'à la mort d'une ressource englobante (H49–H51). Ces états respectent tous les invariants de sûreté ; la charte exclut les interblocages du contrat de sûreté (§4.1). C'est une question d'ergonomie et de progrès, pas de sûreté.

**Options**

1. **Aucune règle** (référence de comparaison). Les blocages sont admis ; les relations persistantes passent par des handles par convention.
2. **Règle locale.** Interdire qu'une opération place une autorité dans un emplacement qu'elle couvre (auto-blocage). O8 l'interdit déjà pour `store` ; le gain à mesurer porte sur `transfer` et `issue`. Ne couvre pas les cycles de longueur ≥ 2 construits par autorité auxiliaire.
3. **`NoLock` global.** Acyclicité de la relation « `b` bloque `a` », auto-blocage défini comme clause séparée, vérifiée à l'arrivée de `transfer`, `issue`, `store`.

**Mesures à produire au jalon 3, pour chaque option :**
- faux rejets sur les cas qui doivent être acceptés : H11, H19, H29b, H35–H37, H44–H47, W1–W3 ;
- blocages résiduels sur H49–H51 ;
- coût d'analyse : la vérification est-elle locale à une fonction, ou exige-t-elle une analyse globale ?

**Critère de choix** : aucune option n'est adoptée si elle rejette un cas qui doit être accepté. Entre options sans faux rejet, la moins coûteuse à analyser l'emporte.

---

## 5b. Scénarios d'usage (exigences de validation, pas une description de l'implémentation actuelle de Weld)

| ID | Structure | Séquence | Attendu |
|---|---|---|---|
| W1 | Graphe de scène | Pool de nœuds `{data, parent : handle, child : handle}` sur une allocation ; deux nœuds liés dans les deux sens par handles ; `resolve` `Modify` d'un nœud, écriture de `data`, `unresolve` ; `freeSlot` d'un nœud encore désigné par le handle de l'autre ; `resolve` de ce handle ; `freeSlot` pendant une résolution active | tout `ok` ; `resolve` du handle périmé : `fail` ; `freeSlot` pendant résolution : `reject` |
| W2 | ECS archetype + sparse set | Archetype à deux colonnes (SoA) sur une allocation ; `split` des colonnes ; système A écrit la colonne 1 pendant que le système B lit la colonne 2 ; `resolveMany` `Modify` de trois entités distinctes d'un pool d'entités ; déplacement d'une entité vers un autre archetype (transferts des champs de la ligne) pendant qu'une vue de colonne est active, puis après sa libération | lectures et écritures disjointes `ok` ; `resolveMany` `ok` ; déplacement pendant la vue : `reject` ; après : `ok` |
| W3 | Arène de frame | `alloc`, `newArena`, trois `issue`, trois vues rangées (`store`) dans une structure locale ; `reset` pendant que les vues vivent ; `endUse` de la structure ; `reset` ; réémission | `reset` pendant : `reject` ; après : `ok` ; réémission `ok` |

## 6. Registre des obligations inter-spécifications

| `stat` (composante concurrente des obligations opaques) ; transférabilité, partageabilité ; H39, H41 | spec 2 |

| `dec` (validité de représentation) ; `SameSizeAlong` ; une référence se range dans un emplacement de type référence ; `kind` comme point d'accroche ; le type d'un pointeur porte la forme d'une région non contiguë (le pointeur n'en désigne que l'adresse la plus basse) | spec 4 |
| `dec` (alignement des accès) ; taille d'un pointeur et encodage `decode` ; largeur des adresses et épuisement de l'espace ; débordement des générations ; placement (`PlacementOK`), jetons (`TokCompat`) | spec 11 |
| Traduction bas niveau de `noalias` | spec 13 |
| Obligation de libération attachée à certains types ; H43 | spécification des ressources |
| `DeclaredDisjoint` (disjonction des feuilles déclarées) ; `FreeCompat` ; représentation des métadonnées d'arène et de pool | bibliothèque |

## 7. Registre de la reconstruction de référence

0. Exécution de MM2-H (17 cas) contre la reconstruction de MM-02 ; MM23-H15 et H16 rejoués après application des décisions 2 et 3 du jalon 2.

import Ern.Corpus.Runner

/-!
# Corpus MM3-H: access discipline, sections A–F, H, I (test module)

The cases of corpus MM3-H of the Jalon 3 material (`ERN_Jalon3_materiel.md`, §1; non-normative
design material), run on the reference kernel and arena of
`specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md` (§60–§78), plus new cases fixed by spec clauses and the
usage scenario W3 (material §5b). This is a test module: no model module imports it.

Each case is a run from `LState.init statics` (§47) by the runner (`Ern.Corpus.Runner`):
`RunsTo k statics os L` states that every step is `ok` and that `L` is library-reachable and its
kernel state `Reachable` (§57). The verdict of the step under test is stated with the relation of
its operation (`DeriveStep`, `TransferStep`, `IssueD`, `ResetD`, …) on the reached state and
decided by `decide`. Each docstring gives the expected verdict from the case's source (the
material, or the spec clause for new cases), the obtained verdict, the class (material §0, rule 5:
`N3` kernel, `Lib` library instance, `spec 3` another specification) and the positive twin (rule 2:
the same sequence without the faulty element, accepted). A case whose obtained verdict differs from
the expected one is kept with its expected verdict and marked **MISMATCH** with its cause; no case
is corrected.

Local shapes are lists of (parent, kind) (§72, §71.1); `lf` is a root leaf, `pt p` a part of `p`.
Place and authority identities are list indices (§38): `enterFrame` appends the locals and one
root authority per root local; `alloc` appends the shape and one root authority; `derive` and
`split` append the derived authorities; `issue` appends one block authority; `reset` appends one
(released) authority.

Not encoded here:
* section G (H30–H34b, H44, handle pools) and the usage scenarios W1, W2 (they use a handle pool):
  later wave (`HandlePool`);
* the cross-registry cases of §56 (a pool and an arena, or two pools, on one `internal`): later
  wave; only the arena registry exists here (`S56`);
* section J, out of the kernel, classified by the material: H38 get-or-insert cache (spec 3,
  flow-sensitive liveness, §25, §32); H39 suspended coroutine holding a `Modify` parameter
  (specs 2 and 3, §29, §81); H40 raw pointer used during a call (spec 3 and the boundary of §19,
  §81); H41 concurrent `writeShared` (spec 2, §18, §24, §68); H42 `defer free(x)` then
  `transfer(x)` (spec 3, `defer` is outside the kernel, §73, §81); H43 resource with a release
  obligation (resource specification, §7).
-/

namespace Ern.Corpus.MM3H

open Ern.MemoryModel.Access Ern.MemoryModel.Arena Ern.Corpus

/-! ## Test contracts and shapes (§48, §72) -/

/-- The empty test contract (§48): nothing shared, pinned, externally done or deallocable. -/
abbrev K0 : K := KD.toK {}

/-- A root leaf of a local shape (§72, §71.1). -/
abbrev lf : Option Nat × Nat := (none, 0)

the view on another value `u`: `ok`. Through a helper on the element, then its `release`, the
configuration is reached (`ok`); then `v` can be neither written, nor relieved of the view, nor
ended (`reject`, §67.1, §62.2, §69.1), while the view stays exercisable in `Observe`; the exit of
the frame is `ok` (§88: residual blocking). **MISMATCH** in form (expected "to arbitrate", obtained
`reject` / `ok`); cause: spec change, spec v0 now determines the verdicts (§65.2, §88). -/
theorem H51 : RunsTo K0 [] h51no h51n ∧ StoreStep 4 4 h51n.kern .reject ∧
    Runs K0 [] (h51p ++ [.derive 2 [2] .observe, .store 4 4]) ∧
    RunsTo K0 [] h51o h51 ∧ (∀ a, Write3Step a [1] h51.kern .reject) ∧
    ReleaseStep 5 h51.kern .reject ∧ EndUseStep K0 1 h51.kern .reject ∧
    h51.kern.ExercisableAt 5 .observe ∧ Runs K0 [] (h51o ++ [.exit]) :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), .reject (by decide), runsTo (by decide), runsTo (by decide),
    write_rejected (by decide), .reject (by decide), .reject (by decide), by decide,
    runsTo (by decide)⟩

/-! ## New cases fixed by spec v0 clauses -/

/-- Prefix of `S63_8` (§72): structure 0 with the part 1, itself with the leaf 2; structure 3
with the part 4, itself with the leaf 5; local 6. -/
def s638p : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, pt 0, pt 1, lf, pt 3, pt 4, lf]]
/-- Run of `S63_8` (§60, §65): 3, `Modify` on the leaf 5, stored into the leaf 2. -/
def s638o : List Op := s638p ++ [.derive 1 [5] .modify, .store 3 2]
/-- State reached by `s638o` (§57). -/
def s638 : LState := final K0 [] s638o

/-- **S63.8** (new case, §63.8; class N3). Transfer self-blocking through a nested part: structure
0 is transferred into structure 3 while its leaf 2 holds 3, which covers the leaf 5 =
`corr(2)`. Expected (§63.8, §88): `reject`. Obtained: `reject` by local self-blocking prevention
alone (§63.1–§63.7 hold). Twin, the stored authority covering the local 6 instead: `ok`. -/
theorem S63_8 : RunsTo K0 [] s638o s638 ∧ corr s638.kern.P 0 3 2 = some 5 ∧
    TransferStep K0 0 3 s638.kern .reject ∧ TransferPreBut638 K0 s638.kern 0 3 ∧
    ¬ NoLocalSelfLock s638.kern 0 3 ∧
    Runs K0 [] (s638p ++ [.derive 2 [6] .modify, .store 3 2, .transfer 0 3]) :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), by decide, .reject (by decide), by decide, by decide,
    runsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- State after the first six steps of `fao`: block 5 on `[5]` issued to 2, so the leaf 5 is not
available (§46, §77). -/
def s772 : LState := final K0 [] (fao.take 6)

/-- **S77.2** (new case, §77.2; class Lib). Issue into a leaf of the region when the region is
unavailable. Expected (§77.2: the condition is static and checked before an availability `fail`):
`reject`. Obtained: `reject` (`issue(0, [5], 5)`: the other static preconditions hold, the
destination is in the region and the region is unavailable). Twin without the faulty element,
the destination 3 outside the region: `fail` (§77.4), as prescribed for an unavailable region;
with an available region (`issue(0, [6], 3)`): `ok`. -/
theorem S77_2 : RunsTo K0 [] (fao.take 6) s772 ∧ IssueD K0 0 [5] 5 s772 .reject ∧
    OptP (s772.arenas[0]?) (fun E => IssueStaticBut s772.kern E [5] 5 ∧
      ¬ IssueStatic s772.kern E [5] 5 ∧ ¬ Avail E [5]) False ∧
    IssueD K0 0 [5] 3 s772 .fail ∧ Runs K0 [] fao :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), rejects (o := .issue 0 [5] 5) (by decide), by decide,
    fails (o := .issue 0 [5] 3) (by decide), runsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- Run of `S77_6` (§60, §65): 5, `Modify` on the value 2 from its root, stored into the storage
leaf 5; the frame's `Modify` on 2 now goes through 5, held by the leaf 5. -/
def s776o : List Op := fao.take 5 ++ [.derive 2 [2] .modify, .store 5 5]
/-- State reached by `s776o` (§57). -/
def s776 : LState := final K0 [] s776o

/-- **S77.6** (new case, §77.6; class Lib). Issue into a destination that would no longer be
exercisable in `Modify`: `issue(0, [5], 2)`. Expected (§77.6, §65.5, §88): `reject`. Obtained:
`reject`; the static checks, availability and the effective right of `internal` hold, but in the
resulting state the block on the leaf 5 makes the frame's only path to 2 (through 5, held by the
leaf 5) circular, so 2 is not under exercisable `Modify`. Twin without the `derive` and `store` of
5: `ok`. -/
theorem S77_6 : RunsTo K0 [] s776o s776 ∧ IssueD K0 0 [5] 2 s776 .reject ∧
    OptP (s776.arenas[0]?) (fun E => IssueStatic s776.kern E [5] 2 ∧ Avail E [5] ∧
      IssueRight s776.kern E [5] ∧ ¬ HasRight (issueKEff s776.kern E [5] 2) .modify 2) False ∧
    Runs K0 [] (fao.take 6) :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), rejects (o := .issue 0 [5] 2) (by decide), by decide, runsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- Run of `S56` (§60, §65): from the arena of `fao` (live, `internal` 4), 5, `Modify` on the
whole storage from `internal`, stored into the value 2. -/
def s56o : List Op := fao.take 5 ++ [.derive 4 [5, 6] .modify, .store 5 2]
/-- State reached by `s56o` (§57). -/
def s56 : LState := final K0 [] s56o

/-- **S56** (new case, §56, §76.4; class Lib). A second arena on the `internal` of a live arena.
Expected (§56, §76.4): `reject`. Obtained: `reject`: every other precondition of `newArena`
holds, the identity 4 is in the arena registry of live administrations. Twin, a distinct
`internal` (5) over the same storage: `ok` (§56: distinct identities are not forbidden merely
because their footprints overlap). The cross-registry cases (a pool and an arena on one
`internal`) belong to the handle-pool wave. -/
theorem S56 : RunsTo K0 [] s56o s56 ∧ NewArenaStep [] 4 4 s56 .reject ∧
    NewArenaBase s56.kern 4 4 ∧ ¬ Guard56 [liveInternals s56.kern s56.arenas] 4 ∧
    Runs K0 [] (s56o ++ [.newArena 4 5]) :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), rejects (k := K0) (o := .newArena 4 4) (by decide), by decide, by decide,
    runsTo (by decide)⟩

/-! ## Usage scenario W3 (material §5b) -/

/-- Run of W3, literal reading (§71, §76, §77, §60, §65): frame 1 with arena value 0, allocator
1, block values 2, 3, 4 and structure 5 (fields 6, 7, 8); storage 9 (leaves 10, 11, 12) owned by
0, `internal` 6; three blocks issued to 2, 3, 4; three views (10, 11, 12), `Observe` on the
blocks, stored into the fields. -/
def w3o : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, lf, lf, lf, pt 5, pt 5, pt 5], .write 1 [1],
  .alloc 1 0 [lf, pt 9, pt 9, pt 9], .write 0 [0], .newArena 9 6, .issue 0 [10] 2,
  .issue 0 [11] 3, .issue 0 [12] 4, .derive 7 [10] .observe, .derive 8 [11] .observe,
  .derive 9 [12] .observe, .store 10 6, .store 11 7, .store 12 8]
/-- State reached by `w3o` (§57). -/
def w3 : LState := final K0 [] w3o
/-- State reached by `w3o` and `endUse` of the structure (§57). -/
def w3e : LState := final K0 [] (w3o ++ [.endUse 5])
/-- Run of W3 with the blocks issued into fields of the structure (§77, §60, §65): structure 2
with the fields 3 to 8; storage 9 (leaves 10, 11, 12), `internal` 3; blocks 4, 5, 6 issued into
the fields 3, 4, 5; views 7, 8, 9 derived from them and stored into the fields 6, 7, 8. -/
def w3vo : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, pt 2, pt 2, pt 2, pt 2, pt 2, pt 2], .write 1 [1],
  .alloc 1 0 [lf, pt 9, pt 9, pt 9], .write 0 [0], .newArena 9 3, .issue 0 [10] 3,
  .issue 0 [11] 4, .issue 0 [12] 5, .derive 4 [10] .observe, .derive 5 [11] .observe,
  .derive 6 [12] .observe, .store 7 6, .store 8 7, .store 9 8]
/-- State reached by `w3vo` (§57). -/
def w3v : LState := final K0 [] w3vo

/-- **W3** (material §5b, frame arena; class Lib, not given by the material). `alloc`,
`newArena`, three `issue`, three views stored into a local structure; `reset` while the views
live; `endUse` of the structure; `reset`; reissue. Expected (material): `reset` during the views
`reject`; after `endUse` of the structure `ok`; reissue `ok`. Obtained, literal reading (blocks
issued to the locals 2, 3, 4): `reject` during the views (§78.2); after `endUse` of the structure,
`reset` is still `reject`, the three blocks being held by the values 2, 3, 4 (§78.2); after their
end, `reset` and the reissue are `ok`. With the blocks issued into fields of the structure: the
expected verdicts (§78.2, §69 effect, §77). **MISMATCH** on the literal reading (after `endUse`
of the structure: expected `ok`, obtained `reject`); cause: case defect, the material does not say
which values hold the blocks. -/
theorem W3 : RunsTo K0 [] w3o w3 ∧ ResetD 0 w3 .reject ∧
    RunsTo K0 [] (w3o ++ [.endUse 5]) w3e ∧ ResetD 0 w3e .reject ∧
    Runs K0 [] (w3o ++ [.endUse 5, .endUse 2, .endUse 3, .endUse 4, .reset 0, .issue 0 [10] 2]) ∧
    RunsTo K0 [] w3vo w3v ∧ ResetD 0 w3v .reject ∧
    Runs K0 [] (w3vo ++ [.endUse 2, .reset 0, .issue 0 [10] 3]) :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), rejects (k := K0) (o := .reset 0) (by decide), runsTo (by decide),
    rejects (k := K0) (o := .reset 0) (by decide), runsTo (by decide), runsTo (by decide),
    rejects (k := K0) (o := .reset 0) (by decide), runsTo (by decide)⟩

end Ern.Corpus.MM3H

import Ern.Corpus.LibRunner

/-!
# Corpus: library cases (test module)

Library cases of the Jalon 3 material (`ERN_Jalon3_materiel.md`; non-normative design material)
and of the corrected handle-pool contract, run on the reference kernel of
`specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md` (§60–§75), the arena of Part XIV (§76–§78), the
handle pool of `Ern.Lib.HandlePool` (contract "HandlePool v0.4 annex", non-normative, corrected by
§36 and §56: composite borrow, `resolveMany` in `Observe` without distinctness, `Modify` right on
the pool value, live pool, `newPool` on `Uninit` storage, `freeSlot` exempting `internal` and its
ancestors) and the stack of `Ern.Lib.DataStack` (contract "DS-v1", non-normative). This is a test
module: no model or library module imports it.

* Section G of corpus MM3-H (material §1 G, handles): H30–H34b, H44.
* Cases of the corrected handle-pool contract: stale, other pool, atomic and distinct batches,
  `resolveMany` in `Observe` with a repeated handle, `freeSlot` with a derived `internal`, under the
  `Modify` right only, on a dead pool, of a free slot; `newPool` on written storage; two pools on
  one storage (`pool_two_freeSlot_cross`).
* The guard of §56 across registries: a second administration (arena, pool, stack) on the
  `internal` of a live administration of another registry, or of the same registry for pools.
* The usage scenarios W1 and W2 of material §5b (W3 is in `Ern.Corpus.MM3H`).

Each case is a run from `CState.init statics` (§47) by the combined runner
(`Ern.Corpus.LibRunner`): `CRunsTo k statics os C` states that every step is `ok`, that `C` is
library-reachable and that its kernel state is reached by kernel steps and ends of slot contents.
The verdict of the step under test is stated with the relation of its operation on the projected
state (`ResolveStep`, `FreeSlotStep`, `NewPoolStep`, `NewArenaStep`, `NewStackStep`, `StoreStep`,
`TransferStep`, …) and decided by `decide`. Each docstring gives the expected verdict from the
case's source, the obtained verdict, the class (material §0, rule 5: `Lib` library instance) and
the positive twin of each rejection or `fail` (rule 2: the same sequence without the faulty
element, accepted). A case whose obtained verdict differs from the expected one keeps its expected
verdict and is marked **MISMATCH** with its cause.

Local shapes are lists of (parent, kind) (§71.1, §72); `lf` is a root leaf, `pt p` a part of
place `p`. Places and authorities are list indices (§38): `enterFrame` appends the locals and one
root authority per local; `alloc` appends the shape and one root authority; `derive` and `split`
append the derived authorities; `issue` appends one block authority; `reset` appends one released
authority; `resolve` appends a companion and an entry authority; `resolveMany` a companion and one
entry authority per handle. Pools and stacks are named by their registry index; a handle is
`⟨pool identity, slot index, generation⟩`.
-/

crunsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- Run of H33 (§72, §71; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1–D.3): frame 1 with the local 0 passes 1,
`Modify` on it, to frame 2, which has the allocator 1, the pool value 2, the handle leaf 3 and the
local 4; storage 5 (entries 6, 7) owned by the pool value, `internal` its root 6; pool 0; slot 0
allocated and resolved: companion 7, entry authority 8. -/
def h33o : List COp := [.enter [] [lf], .derive 0 [0] .modify, .enter [1] [lf, lf, lf, lf],
  .write 2 [1], .write 3 [2], .alloc 1 2 [lf, pt 5, pt 5], .newPool 5 6, .allocSlot 0 3,
  .resolve 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ .modify]
/-- State reached by `h33o` (§57). -/
def h33 : CState := cfinal K0 [] h33o

/-- **H33** (material §1 G, class Lib). A resolved access stored in a value of a frame older than
the pool. Expected (material, anchor order): `reject`. Obtained: `reject`: the effective anchor of
the entry authority 8 is of frame 2, not an ancestor of the frame 1 of the target 0 (§44, §65.4).
Twin, the same `store` into the local 4 of the frame of the pool: `ok`. -/
theorem H33 : CRunsTo K0 [] h33o h33 ∧ StoreStep 8 0 h33.kern .reject ∧
    ¬ EffAnchorOK h33.kern 8 (h33.kern.pframe 0) ∧ CRuns K0 [] (h33o ++ [.store 8 4]) :=
  ⟨crunsTo (by decide), crejects (k := K0) (C := h33) (o := .store 8 0) (by decide), by decide,
    crunsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- **H34** (material §1 G, class Lib). A handle copied (read from 2, written into 3), then two
successive `resolve Modify` of it, with a write of the entry through the first resolution and its
`unresolve` in between. Expected (material): `ok`. Obtained: `ok` at every step (§37, §89: the
handle is data, not an authority; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2). -/
theorem H34 : CRuns K0 [] (pb ++ [.allocSlot 0 2, .read 2 [2], .write 3 [3],
    .resolve 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ .modify, .write 6 [5], .unresolve 5, .resolve 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ .modify]) :=
  crunsTo (by decide)

/-- Run of H34b (§71; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1): a second storage 7 (entries 8, 9) owned by the
pool value 1, its root 5 the `internal` of pool 1, of identity 1; slot 0 of pool 0 allocated. -/
def h34bo : List COp := pb ++ [.alloc 0 1 [lf, pt 7, pt 7], .newPool 7 5, .allocSlot 0 2]
/-- State reached by `h34bo` (§57). -/
def h34b : CState := cfinal K0 [] h34bo

/-- **H34b** (material §1 G, class Lib). A handle of another pool. Expected (material, identity of
the pool; §89): `fail`. Obtained: `fail`: the handle names identity 0, pool 1 has identity 1. Twin,
the same handle on its own pool: `ok`. -/

    HandlePool.ResolveStep 1 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ .modify h34b.toP .fail ∧
    CRuns K0 [] (h34bo ++ [.resolve 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ .modify]) :=
  ⟨crunsTo (by decide), by decide,
    cfails (k := K0) (C := h34b) (o := .resolve 1 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ .modify) (by decide),
    crunsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- Run of H44 (§71, §76–§78; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1–D.3): frame 1 with the arena value 0,
the allocator 1, the pool value 2 and the handle leaves 3 and 4; storage 5 owned by 0, with the
place 6 holding the nodes 7 (fields 8, 9) and 10 (fields 11, 12); arena on 5 (`internal` 5); the
block 6 over the leaves of 6 issued to the pool value; pool on 6 with the block as `internal`;
each node resolved in turn, its link field written, then unresolved; `endUse` of the pool value;
`reset` of the arena. -/
    CRuns KSh [] (pb ++ [.allocSlot 0 2, .derive 1 [1] .modify, .enter [5] [lf],
      .writeShared 5 [1], .allocSlot 0 7, .freeSlot 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩]) :=

/-- Base of `pool_two_freeSlot_cross` (§72, §71, §60, §65; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1): frame 1
with the allocator 0, the pool value 1 and the leaves 2, 3, 4; storage 5 (entries 6, 7) owned by
1, pool 0 on it with `internal` its root 5; then 6, `Modify` on the whole storage from 5, stored
into the leaf 4. -/

/-- State reached by `pxo` (§57). -/
def px : CState := cfinal K0 [] pxo
/-- The twin of `pool_two_freeSlot_cross` continued as the draft witness: pool 1 on `internal` 6
over the same storage; slot 0 allocated in each pool; the leaf 6 written through 6; `freeSlot` of
slot 0 of pool 1. -/

  .freeSlot 1 ⟨1, 0, 0⟩]
/-- State reached by `pxto` (§57). -/
def pxt : CState := cfinal K0 [] pxto

/-- **pool_two_freeSlot_cross** (corrected handle-pool contract, class Lib). A second pool on the
`internal` 5 of the live pool 0, over the same storage, whose `freeSlot` would end the content of a
live slot of pool 0. Expected (§56; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1: "Une autorité ne peut être
`internal` de deux abstractions vivantes"): `reject` at the second `newPool`. Obtained: `reject`;
the other preconditions hold. Twin, the second pool on the distinct `internal` 6 (§56: distinct
identities are not forbidden merely because their footprints overlap): `ok`, and the rest of the
run too. On that twin, the `freeSlot` of pool 1 ends the content of the place 6 (`Init` before,
`Uninit` after), which is the slot 0 of pool 0, still live at generation 0: `internal` 5 of pool 0
is an ancestor of the `internal` 6 of pool 1, hence exempt (D.3). Pool 0 cannot resolve that slot
while pool 1 lives: its `internal` has no effective right on the storage (`reject`, §43 case 3). -/
theorem pool_two_freeSlot_cross : CRunsTo K0 [] pxo px ∧

    CRunsTo K0 [] pxto pxt ∧ (cfinal K0 [] (pxto.take 11)).kern.I 6 = .init ∧
    pxt.kern.I 6 = .uninit ∧
    pxt.pools = [⟨0, 5, 5, [⟨6, 0, true⟩, ⟨7, 0, false⟩]⟩,

import Ern.Corpus.Runner

/-!
# Corpus DataStack: the stack library (test module)

Cases of the library instance `DataStack` of `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md`, run on
the reference kernel (§60–§75) through the library of `Ern.Lib.DataStack`. The spec does not define
the contract (Part XIV preamble: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their
library abstractions and are not defined here"); the contract is DS-v1, non-normative, quoted in the
module docstring of `Ern.Lib.DataStack`. This is a test module: no model or library module imports
it.

* `DOp`: a kernel operation O1–O16 of the corpus runner (`Ern.Corpus.Runner`), or a stack
  operation `newStack`, `push`, `mark`, `rewind`, `grow` (DS-v1).
* `dstep k D o`: the computed outcome (§58); `dstep_sound`: it is an outcome of the relation of the
  operation (`DOpRel`: the kernel relation with the stack metadata unchanged, `NewStackStep`,
  `PushStep`, `MarkStep`, `RewindStep`, `GrowStep`), `ok`, `reject` and `fail` alike.
* `druns`: a run from `DState.init statics` (§47) whose steps are all `ok` reaches a state that is
  library-reachable (`DReach`) and whose kernel state is reachable by O1–O16 (§57,
  `DReach.reachable`).
* `newStack` consults the stack registry and no other (§56, `others = []`): the library states of
  these runs hold no administration other than stacks.

Each case states the reached state with `DRunsTo`, the verdict of the step under test with the
relation of its operation on that state (decided by `decide`; `rewind_dead_fails` adds that `fail`
is the only outcome), and its positive twin (the same sequence without the faulty element,
accepted). Its docstring gives the expected verdict from its source (DS-v1; the brief; the draft
DataStack cases of the derivability material, non-normative), the obtained verdict, the class
(`Lib`: library instance) and the twin. A case whose obtained verdict differs from the expected one
would be kept with its expected verdict and marked **MISMATCH**; there is none.

Readings of DS-v1 (recorded with `Ern.Lib.DataStack`) on which a verdict depends: DS-R5 (`grow` of
a live block that is not the last one: `fail`; the draft rejected) in DS04; DS-R7 (`push` without
room: `fail`) in DS05. Every run uses the representation readings R3 (`rewind` as `split` and

the top; the administrative right of §36 holds where a mark is dead or foreign; a foreign mark is
in no list of the stack; every block grown can be released; the mark removed with an older one is
both later in the list and of a higher top.

Not encoded: the draft `case_rewind_reading` (re-encoded with the library, `Witness.reading_above`);
the draft `case_static_before_fail` other than its `push` without room (its `Init`-destination
conjuncts are changed by §77.2); the kernel `newArena` conjuncts of the draft `case_stacks` (the
stack-library state holds no arena registry; the cross-registry cases of §56 are another module).

import Ern.MemoryModel.Arena
import Ern.MemoryModel.Refinement

/-!
# DataStack: a library administrative abstraction (contract DS-v1, non-normative)

A `DataStack` instance of `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md`. The spec does not define
its contract (Part XIV preamble: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their
library abstractions and are not defined here"). The contract formalized here is the library
contract **DS-v1**, which is **not normative**: every definition below that encodes a DS-v1 item
says so. The normative clauses that constrain it are §36 (`MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable
on the stack value; the abstraction adds no rights to the kernel), §38 and §46 (library state
separate from `S₃`), §47 (empty initial registry), §56 (guard over all registries of live
administrations) and §58 (outcomes).

DS-v1: marks carry the stack identity and a fresh mark identifier; the stack keeps the ordered list
of live marks; `rewind m` fails on a dead or foreign mark, rejects if an active authority derived
from `internal` covers a cell above `m`, otherwise returns those cells to available and removes `m`
and every mark above it; `push` and `grow` use the derived `issue` of Part XIV (`Arena.IssueD`: its
static checks, the availability `fail`, then `split` of `internal` and `store` of the block); `grow`
is in place only (same base, extension into the space directly after the block, `fail` otherwise).

Every `ok` step of the library is a sequence of kernel steps O1–O16 (`DReach.reachable`), so the
abstraction adds no rights to the kernel (§36).
-/

namespace Ern.Lib.DataStack

open Ern.MemoryModel Ern.MemoryModel.Access Ern.MemoryModel.Arena

/-! ## Library state (DS-v1; §38, §46, §47) -/

/-- A block issued by a stack (DS-v1, non-normative; recorded like the issuances of §46): position
`base` of its first cell and number `size` of cells among the ordered cells of the stack, block
authority `auth`, destination `dst` that received it. -/
structure Blk where
  base : Nat
  size : Nat
  auth : Nat
  dst : Nat
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- A mark (DS-v1, non-normative: "marks carry stack identity and a fresh mark identifier";
library metadata of an administrative abstraction, §36, §38): the identity of its stack, its fresh
identifier, the top of the stack when it was taken. -/
structure Mark where
  stack : Nat
  id : Nat
  top : Nat
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- A stack (DS-v1, non-normative; library state, §38, §46): administered storage, `internal`
authority held by the stack value (§36), ordered cells (the leaves of the storage at creation),
top (the cells at positions `≥ top` are available), issued blocks (oldest first), and the ordered
list of live marks (DS-v1: "the stack keeps the ordered list of live marks"). -/
structure Stack where
  storage : Nat
  internal : Nat
  cells : List Nat
  top : Nat
  blocks : List Blk
  marks : List Mark
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- State of the stack library (DS-v1, non-normative; §38: administrative states of library
abstractions are separate from `S₃`): the kernel state, the stack registry (a stack is identified
by its index; stacks are never removed) and the next fresh mark identifier. -/
structure DState where
  kern : S3
  stacks : List Stack
  fresh : Nat

/-- Initial state (§47: the kernel's initial state; the library registry starts empty; DS-v1,
non-normative: no mark identifier given out). -/
def DState.init (statics : Statics) : DState := ⟨S3.init statics, [], 0⟩

/-- The `n` cells from position `b` of the stack, leaves of the administered storage (§46; DS-v1,
non-normative). -/
def cellsOf (st : Stack) (b n : Nat) : List Nat := (st.cells.drop b).take n

## 58. Transition Outcomes

Every operation has a conceptual outcome among:

```text
Outcome3 = ok(new_state) | reject | fail
```

`reject` means that the static discipline does not permit the step; it is neither an implicit runtime trap nor `ub` in the elementary memory machine. `fail` is a **defined failure** leaving the state unchanged; **only `alloc` may produce it in the O1–O16 kernel**. Other kernel operations produce `ok` or `reject`. Library-abstraction operations, including `issue` (§77), may define their own `fail` cases. Where such failure is provided, static preconditions are checked before dynamic availability, according to the operation's contract.

An `ok` transition must satisfy its preconditions, apply exactly its prescribed effects, and preserve the relevant invariants. No transition fabricates a permission to make its conclusion true. Holder and anchor changes are evaluated in the **resulting state** when a rule explicitly so provides.

## 59. Implicit Preservation of Modes and Anchors
# XIV. Arenas and Collective Invalidation — Reference Abstraction

An arena is a **library abstraction**, not a memory-kernel primitive. Operations O17 through O19 are **derived** from operations O1 through O16 and abstraction-specific metadata: `newArena` registers an administration without modifying the kernel; `issue` performs `split` followed by `store` (after checking availability); `reset` performs a `Modify` derivation over all storage—through `derive` or `split`—then `release`, before restoring availability. Their contract below is **normative for the standard-library arena** until Spec 10 takes responsibility for it. It authorizes neither new permissions nor an additional access machine. Arena entries (Section 46) constitute the abstract state of this administration; the guard in Section 56 belongs to its consistency contract. The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and are not defined here.

## 76. O17 — Creation of an Administered Arena

**Preconditions**

1. `storage` is an existing, usable place under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame. It may be local, static, allocated, or a block issued by a previous arena.
2. `internal` is explicitly named by the caller, exists, is active, has own mode `Modify`, and `ExercisableAt(s,internal,Modify)` holds.
3. `internal` is **held by a place**: that place is the arena value; `footprint(internal) = footprint(storage)`.
4. **Unified administration guard (Section 56):** no **live** administrative abstraction, whether an arena or a library instance such as a handle pool, already uses this `internal` identity. The relevant registries of library administrations are consulted before registration. Two distinct identities may cover common leaves: this is not in itself grounds for rejection.
5. All leaves of the arena value holding `internal` are already `Init`; construction does not initialize them implicitly.
6. Dependency, holder, storage, and administration relations respect `WF3`, I1, `AnchorOrder`, `AnchorOrderHeld`, and the expected arena invariants.

**`ok` effect:** A live entry `{storage, internal, available, issued}` is added; the initial `available` set represents the administered storage, and `issued` is initially empty. Registering the entry fabricates no place, access right, or `Init` state. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

The identity of `internal`, not the index of `storage`, is the key to preventing duplication of live administrations. No global constraint requires footprints of live arenas to be pairwise disjoint.

## 77. O18 — Issuing an Arena Block

**Static preconditions**

1. The `arena` entry exists and is live; `internal` is active. `MetaRight` requires exercisable `Modify` over the arena value holding `internal` (Section 36). Mutation of metadata through `writeShared` alone does not satisfy this condition.
2. `region` belongs to the administered storage; `destination` is a usable **leaf** holding no active authority; the destination can legally receive the block value in mode `Modify`. The fact that `destination` is already `Init` is not in itself grounds for rejection, in accordance with O8.2.
   **Local self-blocking prevention: leaf `destination` is not in `region`, including when the region is declared available.** This condition is static and is checked before an availability `fail`.
3. Applicable **static** validity and non-escape restrictions for the destination are satisfied. The `AnchorOrder` check depending on the new anchor is performed on the **simulated resulting state**, after the availability check described in point 4; it cannot turn an unavailable issuance (`fail`) into `reject`.

**Availability and exercisability checks**

4. If static conditions hold but **at least one leaf of `region` does not belong to `available`**, the operation produces **`fail` and leaves the entire state unchanged**. The empty region is always available. An unavailable region does not permit a prior static rejection to be bypassed.
5. If the region is available, the effective mode of `internal` on that region must permit `Modify`; otherwise the outcome is `reject`.
6. The simulated result must satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` **in the resulting state**; moreover, **in that resulting state, `destination` must remain under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame**, in accordance with O8.5. Issuance into a value with a longer lifetime than a local anchor is not made valid merely by storing it in the caller.

**`ok` effect:** A block authority of fresh identity, derived from `internal` and of mode `Modify`, is issued for the region; it is held by `destination`, which receives the corresponding anchor. The leaves of the region leave `available`, and the issuance is added to `issued` with its authority. **Only leaf `destination` becomes `Init`**; no other leaf of the arena value changes initialization. Previous issuances remain intact and valid. Issuance does not automatically install anchors on third-party values: they must use their lawful dependency mechanisms.

**Outcomes:** `ok`, `fail` (region unavailable after static validation), `reject` (static rule, effective right, or anchoring not satisfied). The destination may be a leaf of the arena value itself: its initialization then constitutes **an explicit write to that destination**, not implicit initialization of the entire arena value's metadata.

## 78. O19 — Collective Arena Reset
## 88. Local Self-Blocking and Indirect Cycles

An authority stored by `transfer` in a place that would then become its new holder cannot cover any leaf of that place. Likewise, `issue` cannot issue into a leaf belonging to the issued region, **or into a destination that would no longer be exercisable in `Modify` in the resulting state** (O8.5). These restrictions do not promise general freedom from authority cycles: indirect blocking compatible with safety may remain.

## 89. Handles and Persistent References

In a generation-based pool library abstraction, a handle may contain a logical pool identity, an entry identifier, and a generation. This handle is not, by itself, an access right. Safe resolution temporarily supplies authority when the pool and entry are valid; a stale identity or generation leads to defined failure. These conditions belong to the safe abstraction's contract and do not modify the authority-discipline kernel.
